thread:
ops-bot: 🔔 Paging: cont-batch-tail-latency alert fired for service=runtime-api path=/v1/generate p99_latency=5.8s (SLO 2s) — investigate
Alyssa K: seeing the alert, joining. p95 also elevated (~1.4s -> 2.6s).
Alyssa K: dashboard -> cluster-usw2-contbatch shows simultaneous streaming stalls on GPU nodes 7,8.
Ben R: any deploys in last 30m?
monitoring-bot: No deploys tagged prod in last 60m. Spike correlates with increased mixed-seqlen traffic from org=alpha-corp starting ~T-7m.
Kai M: I can pull traces, starting with a couple of slow requests.
Alyssa K: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce max_batch_size on streaming path, 2) disable mixed-seq grouping, 3) route new traffic to warm pool/dedicated if available. Which is fastest?
Ben R: fastest is reduce max_batch_size and lower batch timeout to force earlier flushes. Can we do that live?
Nadia S: yes, we have runtime flags. I'll push to rolling config on the streaming fleet. Target: max_batch_bytes -> 2MB (from 8MB), batch_window_ms -> 20 (from 50).
Sam T: note that reducing batch size will increase unit cost. We need to balance customer impact vs SLO. Is there clear customer impact?
Priya V: partial. Alpha-corp reported 504s on long streaming responses and our error-rate bumped 0.7% -> 2.9% for their keys. Other customers unaffected so far.
Kai M: pulled a slow trace — big tail at continuous-batcher.WaitForFullBatch where a single long sequence got stuck waiting for short requests to fill the batch. Mixed-seqlen penalty.
Kai M: trace snippet:
```
contbatch_scheduler: try_schedule(batch_id=0x3fa) -> waiters=7
contbatch_window_wait: elapsed_ms=180, max_window_ms=500
kv-cache: hit=false, warm=false
model_infer: batch_size=16, effective_seqlens=[512,32,24,16,8,8,6,6,6,5,4,3,3,2,2,1]
p99_latency=5830ms
```
Alyssa K: that aligns. A single long request plus many tiny ones amplifies padding and waiting. The scheduler is being too patient.
Ben R: propose immediate mitigations: (A) enable seqlen-aware preemption (shed tiny requests to allow long request to run), (B) set conservative per-shard batch cap, (C) route alpha-corp to dedicated small model variant. Which can we do in next 10m?
Nadia S: I can flip seqlen-aware preemption flag to ON in 30s on streaming nodes (flag: `sched.preempt_seqlen = true`). Doing now.
ops-bot: Change request recorded: /ops/flags/sched.preempt_seqlen -> true by Nadia S at 3141592705
Alyssa K: also lower group_by_seq_window to 10ms to reduce wait for grouping. That might prevent mixing extremes.
Priya V: contacting SE for alpha-corp to notify about potential transient errors and to request their non-stream heavy workload be moved to a batch endpoint.
Sam T: monitoring: set a temp alert to p99 > 3.5s with 1m window and paging to this channel.
monitoring-bot: Alert rule updated: p99 > 3.5s (1m) -> channel eng-oncall.
Kai M: after preemption flip and smaller window, I'm seeing immediate drop in queueing on nodes 7/8. p99 trending down to ~2.1s.
Ben R: good. Still worried about tail jitter — need a durable fix. Likely scheduler fairness weights are off; small sequences starving large ones (or vice versa).
Alyssa K: owned follow-ups: 1) mitigate live (Nadia) 2) confirm customer impact + comms (Priya) 3) schedule deeper postmortem on scheduler heuristics (Ben + Kai) 4) consider dynamic batching policy by seqlen buckets (Alyssa)
Nadia S: live config changes applied: `max_batch_bytes=2MB`, `batch_window_ms=20`, `sched.preempt_seqlen=true`, `group_by_seq_window_ms=10`. Rolling across streaming fleet now.
ops-bot: Rolling config change triggered: change_id=chg-3141592710 status=rolling
Kai M: logs after change show fewer long-wait entries. Example entry:
```
contbatch_scheduler: scheduled batch_id=0x42 size=3 elapsed_ms=22
contbatch_run: seqlens=[512,512,512] pad_overhead=0
p99_latency=1180ms
```
Alyssa K: great. Any residual errors?
Priya V: alpha-corp reports degraded but functional streams; error-rate down to 0.9%. They've accepted a short-term mitigation. Will follow up with a support ticket and timeline.
Sam T: let's also enable quick routing rule to divert >95th percentile seqlen requests to dedicated small pool where padding cost is cheaper. Can marketing/devs accept potential cost delta? We'll weigh later.
Ben R: ops TODOs: create a temporary route policy: `route.if(seqlen>400)->dedicated-tiny` and run for 1 hour. I can PR the policy.
Alyssa K: Ben please do the PR. Also add a metric to track fraction of mixed batches and avg padding tokens.
Ben R: PR opened: https://goto/repo/PR-3141 (will merge after smoke).
Kai M: for postmortem: initial hypothesis: mixed-seqlen microbursts exposed scheduler's tradeoff between latency and throughput. Default batch_window and grouping heuristics were tuned for average load, not bursty mixed-length traffic.
Nadia S: we should consider making group_by_seqlen adaptive based on current seqlen variance. Also add a hard cap on wait time for any request (>100ms) to avoid long blocking.
Priya V: customer comms: sent interim note to alpha-corp saying we mitigated and investigating root cause.
Alyssa K: handoff: I'm going offline in ~15m. Ben will take command. Ben, please keep paging policy to critical only and escalate if p99 > 3.5s persists for >5m.
Ben R: taking over. I'll watch for any regressions, verify PR, and coordinate postmortem. Assigning owner: Ben R (incident owner), Postmortem due EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: Incident updated: severity=SEV3 -> mitigation=applied -> owner=Ben R -> incident_id=inc-314159
Sam T: quick note: we should add a synthetic test that simulates mixed seqlen microbursts to catch regressions in CI.
Alyssa K: agreed. Add to eng-infra cadence.
Ben R: closing the live triage. If p99 holds under 2.2s for 10m, we'll mark resolved. Monitoring alarm will auto-close.
monitoring-bot: p99 metric at 3141593220 = 1.98s. Alarm cleared.
Priya V: thanks everyone. I'll follow up on the customer ticket and escalation notes.
Alyssa K: great job. Postmortem/owner Ben R.
Ben R: will run timeline+action items and post into /incidents and ops-runbook.
Nadia S: leaving notes for runtime team: investigate adaptive group_by_seq heuristics, preemptive-shed policies, and explore sequence-length bucketing in batching engine.
Alyssa K: end of thread. :white_check_mark:
